content.text: Workaround via valgrind exception, and leave open to revistit in future months to see if we can remove this workaround cuz fixed in gcc.
Seems this maybe fixed - (tested on  ubuntu 1910) - so retesting more widely.
RE-ENABLE, bug still exists in 1804 (and I think 1810). Fixed in 1904. Revisit when we lose support for ubuntu 1804.
Verified 2020-11-24: this is still required on Ubuntu 18.04.
Seems fixed on all subsequent (20.04 and 20.10) releases.

I reviewed the calls. The complaint is about the call
void String::AsNarrowString (const locale& l, string* into) const
Execution::Throw (Execution::StringException (L"Error converting locale multibyte string to UNICODE"));
I verified the docs - say to read from arg2 to arg3 (range) and those are valid strings. I experiemnted with fake enlarging the buffer and that mitigated/hid the issue, but there is no reason.
This is just a bad warning, or rather awarning about a probable bug with libstdc++.
NOTE from the changelog from gcc 7.2.0
src/c++11/codecvt.cc (range): Add non-type template parameter and
define oerloaded operators for reading and writing code units.
(range<Elem, false>): Define partial specialization for accessing
wide characters in potentially unaligned byte ranges.
and this issue just appeared in the latest version of ubuntu - 17.10 - using gcc 7.2.0.
